As we wrap up our time with *The Seven Storey Mountain* by Thomas Merton, let’s pause and take in what this journey really means for you and me. This isn’t just one man’s search for God—it’s a reflection for anyone who’s ever longed for meaning, belonging, or a little more peace. Life’s journey, as Merton shows us, isn’t a straight climb. There are losses, moments of rebellion, doubts, and times when surrender feels like the only way forward. The monastery, with all its silence and routine, becomes a place of transformation—not a way to run from the world, but a way to truly see it, and ourselves, with fresh eyes.
So, what can we take with us? Real belonging isn’t about being perfect—it’s about showing up honestly and loving those around you, just as they are. Finding meaning? It’s less about collecting the right answers, and more about letting go, opening up, and being willing to grow. Stillness and silence—those moments we often avoid—can actually uncover what’s stirring deep in your heart. And faith? It comes alive not because we never struggle, but because we keep showing up, even after we fall, ready to begin again. When you’re rooted in contemplation and love, service and kindness just flow naturally.
So, if you ever feel restless, uncertain, or like something’s missing—know you’re not alone. The journey isn’t about reaching some perfect destination. It’s about learning to walk forward with openness, trust, and a willingness to let your questions shape you. Every doubt, every struggle, those aren’t roadblocks—they’re invitations. Opportunities to discover who you really are, and who you’re meant to become. Just like the young man in this story, you might find that peace isn’t about escaping the world, but embracing it with a new heart. So take your next step, even if it’s small. Trust that you don’t have to climb the mountain alone. The path can be steep, but with each new height, the view gets better—and it’s worth every step.
